definitions.explanation: To a striking or notable degree. The adverbial form of the i-adjective 著しい. Used in formal and written contexts to describe changes, differences, or developments that are clearly evident.

examples.japanese: {技術|ぎじゅつ}が{著|いちじる}しく{進歩|しんぽ}した。
{成績|せいせき}が{著|いちじる}しく{低下|ていか}している。
{公正|こうせい}さを{著|いちじる}しく{欠|か}く{判断|はんだん}だと{批判|ひはん}された。
examples.english: It was criticized as a judgment that conspicuously lacked fairness.

notes: The adverbial form of {著|いちじる}しい (remarkable, conspicuous). Frequently appears in formal writing, news, and legal/academic texts. Common collocations: {著|いちじる}しく{増加|ぞうか}する (increase remarkably), {著|いちじる}しく{低下|ていか}する (decline significantly), {著|いちじる}しく{欠|か}く (conspicuously lack). In legal contexts, {著|いちじる}しく{不当|ふとう} means 'grossly unfair' and is a standard legal phrase.
